I audited this assuming it was wrong. It holds up.

**Question fidelity** — I read page 4 through all three channels myself. The text matches the brief verbatim; the render confirms the bold+underlined **additional** on the misprediction bullet (which the text channel flattens); `manifest.json` genuinely reports `n_images: 0` / `figures: []` for every page, so channel 3 is legitimately empty rather than skipped. The page-1 hint the worker cites — "cache miss penalty (transfer time) is an additional cost on top of the hit time" — is real and verbatim, and it does independently justify the additive AMAT model. No brief/page discrepancy.

**Numbers** — I re-ran `verify.py` in my own dir: output is byte-identical to the captured `verify_out.txt`, so it isn't stale. I then recomputed the whole thing from scratch in `fractions.Fraction` without reusing the worker's model: baseline 8/5 = 1.6 ns, target 38/25 = 1.52 ns, threshold (2.6−1.52)/1.1 = 54/55 = 0.981818…, and an exact-rational grid sweep bottoming out at 0.981819. Agrees. The rounding finding is real: 98.18% gives 1.52002 ns and violates the bound, 98.19% gives 1.51991 ns and satisfies it, so rounding up is correct. The 6.25% perfect-predictor ceiling checks out too — the answer is tight but the tightness is in the problem, not the arithmetic. Every number in `answer.tex` traces to a computed line.

**LaTeX** — compiled the fragment in my own minimal wrapper: two clean passes, no warnings, no undefined refs. No `\documentclass`/`\usepackage`/`document` env. All 7 labels namespaced `p3:eq:*`. I rendered the PDF and read it, including a 260 dpi upscaled crop of the derivation — the align blocks, the 108/110 = 54/55 chain and the repeating-decimal overlines all set correctly.

**Hygiene** — `lint_output.py` exits 0; OUTPUT holds exactly `answer.tex` + `preamble.txt`; `downloads.md` says nothing installed and I confirmed there's no venv or downloaded artifact in the playground.

Two minor defects, neither worth another round: a leaked tool-call artifact (`</content>`, `</invoke>`) at the end of `notes.md` (playground-only, no R4 impact), and `preamble.txt` requesting `amssymb` that `answer.tex` never uses (harmless, master de-dupes).

The one real judgement call — reading "worst case" as 2.1 ns rather than 52.1 ns — I examined and accepted: the blank asks what "a cache access takes", the two way-prediction bullets are exactly the two access times, and A's values are the inputs B's access-time term needs. The worker states the reading in `answer.tex` so a grader can see it. Full reasoning is in `validators/p3/checklist.md`.

VERDICT: PASS
